'''Canad Corporation of Manitoba Ltd.''' is a Winnipeg-based [[Hospitality industry|hospitality]] company. It owns or operates ten [[Hotel|hotels]] in Canada and one in the United States, with all but one of its properties (a [[Radisson Hotels|Radisson]] hotel in downtown Winnipeg) operating under the '''Canad Inns Destination Centre''' branding.

Alongside its hotels, it also operates a number of [[restaurant]], [[tavern]], and event venues—most of which co-located as part of Canad Inns locations.

==Company overview==
Canad Inns operates a total of 10 properties in the province and one in the US. <ref name=Stay>{{cite web|title=Stay|url=http://www.canadinns.com/stay/|publisher=Canad Inns|access-date=24 January 2013}}</ref> Canad Inns also operates restaurants, pubs, night clubs, water parks, and first class banquet and conference facilities within its hotel complexes, which are branded as "destination centres."

Several of Canad Inns destination centres are located adjacent to larger venues. Canad Inns Brandon is located adjacent to the [[Keystone Centre]], one location is attached to Winnipeg's [[Club Regent Casino]], while the [[Grand Forks, North Dakota]] location is connected to the [[Alerus Center]]. In 2013, Canad Inns opened a $40 million location at Winnipeg's [[Health Sciences Centre (Winnipeg)|Health Sciences Centre]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ltd |first=Kostuch Media |date=2013-03-18 |title=Canad Inns Opens at Winnipeg Health Sciences Centre |url=https://www.hoteliermagazine.com/canad-inns-opens-at-winnipeg-health-sciences-centre/ |access-date=2024-05-27 |website=Hotelier Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref>

The company also owns the historic [[Metropolitan Theatre (Winnipeg)|Metropolitan Theatre]] building in downtown Winnipeg and has converted it into a multi-purpose entertainment and banquet facility.

The chain employs more than 3,500 people and is the 14th largest hotel chain in Canada and the largest in Manitoba.<ref>{{cite web|title=Careers|url=http://www.canadinns.com/careers/|publisher=Canad Inns|access-date=24 January 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Canada Inns|url=http://www.economicdevelopmentwinnipeg.com/uploads/document_file/canad_inns_corporation_company_profile.pdf|access-date=24 January 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304030018/http://www.economicdevelopmentwinnipeg.com/uploads/document_file/canad_inns_corporation_company_profile.pdf|archive-date=4 March 2016|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref>

In 2000, Canad Inns was named one of "Canada's 50 Best Managed Companies."<ref>[https://www.canadas50best.com/en/meetourwinners/Pages/2000winners.aspx 50 best Managed Companies in 2000] {{dead link|date=July 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> In 2009 and 2010, Canad Inns was named one of Manitoba's Top 25 Employers as published by the Winnipeg Free Press.<ref>[http://www.eluta.ca/top-employer-canad-inns Canad Inns - Top Employer]</ref>

==Sponsorships==
In 2001, the company purchased the naming rights to Winnipeg Stadium, home of the [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]] of the [[Canadian Football League]], after which the stadium became known as [[Canad Inns Stadium]]. The stadium was demolished in 2013.

==Litigation==
In 2007, Lake Louise Limited Partnership filed suit alleging that Canad inflated management fees owed to it for operating Club Regent Casino Hotel and Canad Inns Brandon by including every dollar deposited in video lottery terminals (VLTs) as gross revenue.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/manitoba/canad-inns-forced-to-pay-back-management-fees-1.2852990| title = Canad Inns forced to pay back management fees {{!}} CBC News}}</ref>

In November 2014, the receiver for the failed Crocus Investment Fund petitioned a court to dissolve and liquidate the parent company of Canad Inns, alleging Canad Corporation assets to have been wrongfully diverted for company president Leo Ledohowski's benefit.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/manitoba/crocus-asks-court-to-sell-off-canad-inns-assets-1.2849321| title = Crocus asks court to sell off Canad Inns assets {{!}} CBC News}}</ref> In November 2019, the court-appointed receiver [[Deloitte]] reached an agreement to resolve the lawsuit, under which Canad agreed to pay $4 million—accounting for most of the fund's original investment.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-02-03 |title=Canad Inns pays back $4M to Crocus Fund, ending decade-long dispute with receiver |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/manitoba/canad-inns-crocus-fund-4-million-1.5449063 |access-date=2024-05-26 |website=CBC News}}</ref>

In December 2014, the company was also sued by former chief operating officer Antonio Ventresca and his wife for [[wrongful dismissal]], alleging that Ledohowski sexually harassed her while the pair were working for the company, and that it "engaged in a course of reprisal" after she refused Ledohowski's advances over a year-long period—leading to their firing.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2014-12-08 |title=Lawsuit accuses Canad Inns owner Leo Ledohowski of sexual harassment |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/manitoba/lawsuit-accuses-canad-inns-owner-leo-ledohowski-of-sexual-harassment-1.2865126 |access-date=2024-05-26 |website=CBC News}}</ref>

A lawsuit against Leo Ledohowski, Canad Inns Group and Fillmore Riley LLP was filed by Leo's brother, former Vice President, working partner and Co-founder commenced in June 2021 and remains active.
